messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: prod-us-east decode p99 > 2s for model 'redwood-v2-small'. Paging events + kernel page faults detected. Auto-runbook invoked: https://rwd.internal/runbooks/paging-kernel. Root ts=3132109876
ashley (oncall): acknowledged, jumping in. seeing p95->~850ms, p99 spikes 1.8-2.3s. Streaming tailers showing stalls and repeated GC-like free/alloc logs in nodes A/C.
miguel (sre): confirming traces — high stall counts correlate with kernel update rolled at ~3132109000 (kernel: flashquant-v1.2 + compiler flag -O3-quant). Also NVFlashAttn enabled in runtime.
sofia (runtime): I merged the FlashQuant kernel PR last night, small perf gains in perf tests but we turned on an allocator tweak that changed page residency heuristics. PR: https://rwd.internal/prs/9221.
ashley (oncall): important: which clusters impacted? I see prod-us-east (primary) and prod-eu-west maybe a bit. customer-facing: beta-corp and analytics-batch have elevated error rates (rate-limited retries).
miguel (sre): impact summary from metrics: token throughput down ~15% overall, tail latency p99 anomaly +300% on streaming endpoints. Paging-induced stalls causing decode coroutine backlog.
kevin (infra): we should roll the kernel back on the hot pool. Suggest pinning to kernel flashquant-v1.0 across prod-us-east for now and scale prewarmed containers.
sofia (runtime): agree. Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback kernel to v1.0 2) disable NVFlashAttn flag 3) route streaming traffic to dedicated prewarmed pool with quantized model variant.
miguel (sre): doing staged rollback via fleet-api. Command to pin kernels for a given pool:
```
# example (run as infra-deploy)
curl -X POST https://internal-api/fleet/pools/pin -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"pool":"prod-us-east-hot","kernel":"flashquant-v1.0"}'
```
ashley (oncall): running rollback now on one shard to confirm. will post results.
ashley (oncall): rollback started on shard A at 3132110005. patch applied, restarting runtime.
ops-runbook-bot: Automatic step: scaled prewarm pools +20% for prod-us-east-hot at 3132110030. Logs: https://rwd.internal/logs/rollscale/3132110030
ashley (oncall): shard A p95 dropped back to ~120ms, p99 to ~240ms after rollback. Shard B still elevated.
miguel (sre): good sign. initiate rolling rollback across remaining hot shards. I will coordinate and throttle to avoid capacity cliffs.
sofia (runtime): follow-up: we'll also flip the runtime flag for NVFlashAttn to false in canary to validate behavior before re-enabling. flag path: /service/runtime/flags/nvflashattn=false
kevin (infra): adding traffic routing change: divert non-critical streaming to dedicated-reserved pool to reduce pressure on hot pools. command:
```
# routing move
internalctl route-set --from cluster:prod-us-east --to pool:dedicated-streaming --filter "model:redwood-v2-small and priority!=critical"
```
ashley (oncall): customer impact: beta-corp reports 35-45% retry rate on long streaming sessions. notif to CSM/sales: pinged @sales-ops, raised support ticket SUP-45221.
sofia (runtime): quick root-cause hypothesis: allocator residency change in flashquant-v1.2 + NVFlashAttn path causes higher page refaults for long KV cache traces, leading to stalls in decode loop for streaming where KV cache thrashing is common.
miguel (sre): agree. we'll collect: perf counters, page-fault histograms, runtime traces. attaching triage checklist to incident: https://rwd.internal/incidents/3132109876/triage
ashley (oncall): ongoing mitigation: rolling rollback in progress (50% shards done). will monitor p95/p99 for 15m windows.
ops-runbook-bot: Automated customer impact summary generated and sent to #support (ticket SUP-45221) at 3132110200.
kevin (infra): after rollback completes, plan: create a controlled canary enabling NVFlashAttn + allocator tweak with extended KV cache load tests, and a longer soak before wider rollout.
sofia (runtime): logging note: capture a full debug dump for two affected shards and leave verbose pagefault logs on for 2 hours: /tmp/incident-3132109876-dump.
miguel (sre): monitoring: setting alerts to tighten SLO windows: p95 > 300ms or p99 > 800ms triggers pager.
ashley (oncall): handoff: my shift ends in 45m. miguel will take overnight watch once rollback completes. I created an incident bridge: https://rwd.internal/bridges/3132109876 and a JIRA incident: RWDINC-1207.
miguel (sre): taking handoff. will continue rolling rollback and validate cluster-wide metrics. will post an interim update in 30m and then on hourly cadence until stabilized.
ashley (oncall): logging final for my handoff: actions taken: 1) pinned kernel -> flashquant-v1.0 on hot pool (rolling) 2) scaled prewarm +20% 3) routed non-critical streaming to dedicated pool 4) filed SUP-45221 + JIRA RWDINC-1207 5) started debug dumps.
sofia (runtime): postmortem TODOs: revert allocator tweak in kernel tree, add KV-cache-heavy soak tests, improve canary gating for allocator flags, add guardrail to runtime to fallback away from NVFlashAttn on >x% page-faults.
miguel (sre): noted. I'll own the overnight monitoring and coordinate the postmortem with runtime eng. Thanks all — handing this to pager oncall rotation. :thumbsup:
ashley (oncall): thanks team, handing off now. :white_check_mark:
